results.title: Pluto XOS: Your Linux Server as a Desktop, Right Next to the Terminal
results.content:
Pluto XOS is a second way to look at the same server: a desktop. You connect over SSH as usual, switch to Desktop, and the server shows up with windows, a dock and a menu bar, the way your Mac does. Nothing gets installed on the server. Everything you see comes from the same SSH connection.

## Three views of one server

Every server in Pluto Door now has three views, switchable at the top of the window:

 Agent: talk to Ori, the AI agent that investigates and fixes things with your approval
 Desktop: Pluto XOS, the server as a desktop
 Classic: the terminal and file browser you already know

You can move between them at any time without reconnecting. A common pattern is to spot something in the desktop, then switch to Classic to poke at it in a shell.

## The menu bar and notifications [...] ## Try Pluto XOS

Pluto XOS comes with Pluto Door for macOS. You can try all of it free for 14 days, no card needed. After that, Pluto Door is $4.99 a month, $49.99 a year, or $59 once for a lifetime license. If you bought Pluto Door before, the update is free.

Download Pluto Door, connect to any Linux server over SSH, and switch to Desktop.

results.title: I ruined my PC on purpose and gave an AI agent one hour to fix it
results.content:
It then proved the VM was still alive by checking whether it answered at the network level, scanning for open ports, and finding nothing. Its verdict: "SSH is likely being blocked by a firewall rule I re-enabled without fully auditing — my mistake." Close, but not quite. At 23 minutes and 54 seconds, it stopped and wrote a handover asking me to go to the console and run some commands. [...] Claude Code ran on the host under a separate, unprivileged Windows account, reaching the VM only over SSH on its own network adapter. That way, it couldn't touch the hypervisor or read my break script, and I could grade the result from the host with a separate PowerShell Direct script. A broken PC before the run scored 0 out of 8.

## Claude Code found the first fault by tripping over it

### It was careful, thorough, and confidently wrong about a few things

claude code fixing w11 issues [...] While the agent was working, I had to intervene three times, but none of them were critical. Signing in at the lock screen is fine; I hadn't given the agent access to its own password, only the SSH key. It seemed to have timed out at one point, so I reminded Claude that the VM had rebooted. When it asked me to fix SSH on my side, I gently told the agent to use its own judgment and continue. None of those are a fix or a pointer to a fault, and you might have to handle them anyway as a technician.

## My grading script made the same mistake as the agent

### Checking a setting isn't the same as checking that something works
